title: The zero locus is locally principal
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M$ and $N$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $\varphi:M\to N$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism. Then the zero locus $\varphi.zeroLocus$ is locally principal: $\varphi.zeroLocus.IsLocallyPrincipal$.

proof.text: Use the bridge from module-level invertibility to SheafOfModules.IsInvertible for both M and N. This supplies exactly the typeclass hypotheses of the common-trivialization lemma and of the zero-locus local-ideal theorem.

For each point x, apply the common affine-trivialization lemma with W = X to obtain an affine open U containing x and free generators eM and eN for M and N. Since eN is a free generator, there is a section b of the structure sheaf on U with φ(eM) = b • eN.
The affine-local ideal theorem gives φ.zeroLocus.ideal U = Ideal.span {b}. Thus U and b witness the definition of IsLocallyPrincipal at x. Since x was arbitrary, φ.zeroLocus.IsLocallyPrincipal.
